reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: Hypoplasia or absence of the fifth finger or toe nail and distal phalanx is the classical, though not universal, hand and foot finding
The facial gestalt is coarse with a wide mouth, thick lips, broad nasal tip, long philtrum and thick eyebrows, often with generalised hirsutism but sparse scalp hair
Caused by variants in genes encoding subunits of the BAF (SWI/SNF) chromatin-remodelling complex, most commonly ARID1B
Developmental delay and intellectual disability, usually with speech more affected than motor skills, are consistent features
Feeding difficulty, hypotonia and frequent infections are common in early childhood
Corpus callosum abnormalities and other structural brain findings may be seen on neuroimaging
Inheritance is autosomal dominant, and nearly all cases result from de novo variants
reference.pathophysiology: Coffin-Siris syndrome is a BAFopathy caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding components of the BAF (SWI/SNF) ATP-dependent chromatin-remodelling complex, including ARID1B, ARID1A, SMARCB1, SMARCA4 and SMARCE1. This complex repositions nucleosomes to make DNA accessible for transcription, and is essential for regulating gene-expression programmes during development. Disruption of its subunits alters chromatin accessibility and downstream developmental gene networks, impairing neuronal, craniofacial and limb development and producing the characteristic dysmorphism, digital anomalies and cognitive impairment.
additionalDifferentials: Mabry syndrome and other coarse-facies intellectual disability disorders
additionalInvestigations: Gene-panel or exome sequencing covering ARID1B, ARID1A, SMARCB1, SMARCA4, SMARCE1 and related BAF genes
Chromosomal microarray to detect deletions involving ARID1B
Brain MRI to assess the corpus callosum and other structural anomalies
Renal tract ultrasound for structural anomalies
redFlags: Failure to thrive from severe feeding difficulty requiring nutritional support
Recurrent severe infections suggesting immune vulnerability
Undiagnosed congenital heart disease causing cardiorespiratory compromise
reference.prognosis: Most individuals have mild to moderate intellectual disability and survive into adulthood; outlook depends on the severity of associated malformations and the specific gene involved, with some subunit variants carrying more severe phenotypes. Speech and communication support can substantially improve function.
pitfalls: Excluding the diagnosis when the fifth-nail finding is absent, as it is not universal
Confusing it with Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome, which shares BAF-complex biology but has distinct features
Overlooking a corpus callosum anomaly that informs prognosis and counselling
Assuming a single gene test suffices rather than covering the full BAF panel
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
